messages.author: c6c2f8b68485ba9a
messages.subject: Issues regarding SECR model extrapolation
parts:
Dear Dr. Efford & Members of the Group,

I am trying to run SECR with covariates for a landscape with five different sites, out of which only one was sampled with camera traps. I want to extrapolate the density in the rest of the sites using habitat covariates (as the habitat is similar to the sampled site and known to inhabited by the study species). However, when I am trying to make the capture history, it shows the an error (although the traps match with the capture file): 
"Error in make.capthist(capture.fil, cameratrap) :
  failed to match some capture locations to detector sites"
I can't figure out what I'm doing wrong. I would be grateful if you could review the issue and help me find a solution. I am attaching the code in case it helps.
Thank you.

Code
library(secr)
library(sf)
tmp <- read.csv("trap1.csv",head = T)

#reading trap file
cameratrap <- read.traps(data = tmp[,2:4], trapID = 'trapid', detector = "count")
usage(cameratrap) <- tmp[,5:48]
row.names(cameratrap) <- tmp$trapid
cameratrap <- split(cameratrap, tmp$Site)
#reading capture file
capture.fil <- read.csv("capture1.csv", head = T)

#with occasions
CH <- make.capthist(capture.fil)
summary(CH, terse = T)

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Issues regarding SECR model extrapolation
parts:
Hello Ayan

Using the data you sent offline it seems -
capture.fil has a single 'session'
cameratrap is a list

So to read with make.capthist() you need only the first component of the list, something like
CH <- make.capthist(capture.fil, cameratrap[[1]])

This gives me
summary(CH, terse = T)
Occasions Detections Animals Detectors
44 193 99 712

More generally - if you have data for only one area you can simply fit the model in that area, ignoring all the rest, and later extrapolate using predictDsurface and a different (larger) mask with any necessary covariates.

Murray
